ab-test.label: A/B test
ab-test.definition: A controlled experiment that randomly splits users into a control group and one or more treatment groups, then compares an outcome metric between them.

p-value.label: p-value
p-value.definition: The probability of seeing a result at least as extreme as the one observed if there were truly no effect. It is not the probability that the result is a fluke.

lift.label: Lift
lift.definition: The relative improvement of the treatment over control on a metric, for example (treatment minus control) divided by control.

statistical-significance.label: Statistical significance
statistical-significance.definition: A result is called significant when its p-value falls below a threshold chosen in advance, commonly 0.05. It says the data would be unlikely if there were no effect, not that the effect is large or important.

type-i-error.label: Type I error
type-i-error.definition: A false positive: concluding there is an effect when there isn't one. The significance level sets how often you accept this.

type-ii-error.label: Type II error
type-ii-error.definition: A false negative: missing an effect that is really there. Its rate is one minus the test's power.

sample-size.label: Sample size
sample-size.definition: How many observations an experiment needs to reliably detect an effect of a chosen size. It depends on the baseline rate, the variance, and the error rates you accept.

default-rate.label: Default rate
default-rate.definition: The share of borrowers who fail to repay a loan within a defined period.

confidence-interval.label: Confidence interval
confidence-interval.definition: A range computed with a procedure that, over many repeated studies, would contain the true value a stated share of the time, for example 95%.

bootstrapping.label: Bootstrapping
bootstrapping.definition: Estimating uncertainty by repeatedly resampling your own data with replacement and recomputing a statistic each time.

simpsons-paradox.label: Simpson's paradox
simpsons-paradox.definition: A pattern where a trend that appears in several subgroups reverses or disappears when the groups are combined.

customer-segmentation.label: Customer segment
customer-segmentation.definition: A group of customers treated as similar for analysis, for example by size, region or behavior.

xgboost.label: XGBoost
xgboost.definition: A popular gradient-boosting library that builds many small decision trees in sequence, each one correcting the errors of the ones before it.

gradient-boosting.label: Gradient boosting
gradient-boosting.definition: An ensemble method that adds models one at a time, each trained to reduce the error that remains in the combined model so far.

logistic-regression.label: Logistic regression
logistic-regression.definition: A linear model for classification that outputs a probability. It is simple, fast and easy to explain.

auc.label: AUC
auc.definition: Area under the ROC curve: the chance that the model scores a random positive example above a random negative one. 0.5 is chance and 1.0 is perfect ranking.

test-set.label: Test set
test-set.definition: Data held back from training and used only to estimate how the model will perform on new data.

production-model.label: Model in production
production-model.definition: A model serving real predictions to real users or downstream systems, as opposed to being evaluated offline.

model-drift.label: Model drift
model-drift.definition: Decline in a deployed model's performance over time because the world, or the data it sees, has changed since it was trained.

model-degradation.label: Model degradation
model-degradation.definition: A measurable drop in a deployed model's quality compared with when it launched, whatever the cause.

monitoring.label: Model monitoring
monitoring.definition: Tracking a deployed model's inputs, predictions and outcomes to catch problems early.

alerting.label: Alerting
alerting.definition: Automatic notifications when a monitored value crosses a threshold, so someone can act.

cash-collection-forecast.label: Cash collection forecast
cash-collection-forecast.definition: A prediction of when, and how much of, the money owed on invoices will actually be received.

cash-flow-forecast.label: Cash flow forecast
cash-flow-forecast.definition: A prediction of the money coming in and going out over a future period.

forecast-horizon.label: Forecast horizon
forecast-horizon.definition: How far into the future a forecast looks, for example 90 days or 12 months. Accuracy generally worsens as the horizon grows.

forecasting.label: Forecasting
forecasting.definition: Predicting future values of a quantity from past data and known drivers.

time-series.label: Time series
time-series.definition: Data recorded over time in order, where the sequence matters because observations are usually related to nearby ones.

backtesting.label: Backtesting
backtesting.definition: Evaluating a forecasting method by replaying history: at each past date, use only what was known then, predict forward, and compare with what happened.

cross-validation.label: Cross-validation
cross-validation.definition: Estimating performance by training and evaluating on several different splits of the data and averaging the results.

k-fold.label: k-fold
k-fold.definition: A cross-validation scheme that splits the data into k parts and takes turns holding each one out for evaluation.

feature-engineering.label: Feature engineering
feature-engineering.definition: Turning raw data into inputs a model can learn from, such as ratios, counts over a time window or encoded categories.

feature-importance.label: Feature importance
feature-importance.definition: A score for how much each input feature contributes to a model's predictions. Different methods can rank the same features differently.

data-pipeline.label: Data pipeline
data-pipeline.definition: A sequence of automated steps that moves data from its sources, transforms it, and delivers it for use, such as model training.

data-validation.label: Data validation
data-validation.definition: Automated checks that data meets expectations (types, ranges, missing values, freshness) before it is used.

data-quality.label: Data quality
data-quality.definition: How well data fits its purpose: accurate, complete, consistent, timely and free of unwanted duplicates.

churn.label: Churn
churn.definition: When a customer stops using or paying for a product. The churn rate is the share lost in a period.

cohort.label: Cohort
cohort.definition: A group of users who share a starting point, typically the period they signed up, tracked together over time.

retention.label: Retention
retention.definition: The share of a group that is still active some time after they started.

window-function.label: Window function
window-function.definition: A SQL function that computes a value for each row using a set of related rows (its window) without collapsing them into one row.

top-n-per-group.label: Top N per group
top-n-per-group.definition: A common SQL pattern: keep only the N highest-ranked rows within each group, such as each department.

rolling-average.label: Rolling average
rolling-average.definition: An average over a sliding window of recent values, used to smooth out day-to-day noise.

sessionization.label: Sessionization
sessionization.definition: Grouping a stream of user events into sessions, usually by starting a new one after a long enough gap.

anti-join.label: Anti-join
anti-join.definition: A query that returns the rows in one table that have no match in another.

pandas-merge.label: pandas merge
pandas-merge.definition: Combining two DataFrames on matching key columns, like a SQL join.

deduplication.label: Duplicate records
deduplication.definition: Multiple rows that refer to the same real-world entity. What counts as a duplicate depends on the business definition.

bias-variance-tradeoff.label: Bias-variance tradeoff
bias-variance-tradeoff.definition: The tension between a model too simple to capture the pattern (bias) and one so flexible that it fits noise in the training data (variance).

evaluation-metric.label: Evaluation metric
evaluation-metric.definition: A number that summarizes how well a model performs, such as accuracy, precision, recall or AUC. Each one rewards different behavior.

accuracy.label: Accuracy
accuracy.definition: The share of predictions that are correct.

fraud-detection.label: Fraud detection
fraud-detection.definition: Identifying transactions or accounts that are deliberately deceptive. Fraud is rare, and fraudsters adapt.

missing-data.label: Missing data
missing-data.definition: Values that are absent from a dataset. Why they are missing affects how they should be handled.

outliers.label: Outliers
outliers.definition: Values far from the rest of the data. They can be errors or genuinely rare events.

experimentation-platform.label: Experimentation platform
experimentation-platform.definition: Shared infrastructure that assigns users to experiment variants, logs exposure and reports results, so teams can run A/B tests consistently.

batch-processing.label: Batch processing
batch-processing.definition: Computing over accumulated data on a schedule, such as nightly.

stream-processing.label: Stream processing
stream-processing.definition: Computing on events continuously as they arrive.

feature-pipeline.label: Feature pipeline
feature-pipeline.definition: The data flow that computes the inputs a model uses, both for training and for live predictions.

real-time.label: Real-time
real-time.definition: Responding within a tight latency bound, typically milliseconds to a few seconds, as each request arrives.

recommendation-system.label: Recommendation system
recommendation-system.definition: A system that suggests items a user is likely to want, using their history and the behavior of similar users.

ml-intake.label: ML intake process
ml-intake.definition: The way a company collects, evaluates, prioritizes and approves requests for machine learning work.

algorithmic-fairness.label: Algorithmic fairness
algorithmic-fairness.definition: Whether a model's decisions treat groups of people equitably. There are several competing definitions, and they cannot all be satisfied at once.

disparate-impact.label: Disparate impact
disparate-impact.definition: When a decision process affects one group at a materially different rate than another, even without using a protected attribute directly.

model-rollout.label: Model rollout
model-rollout.definition: Moving a new model into live use, from limited exposure up to full traffic.

unit-testing.label: Unit test
unit-testing.definition: An automated test of one small piece of code against an expected result.

training-serving-skew.label: Training-serving skew
training-serving-skew.definition: A mismatch between how features are computed or distributed during training and during live prediction.

reproducibility.label: Reproducibility
reproducibility.definition: Being able to rerun an analysis or model and obtain the same result.

model-serving.label: Model serving
model-serving.definition: Running a trained model so that other systems can request predictions from it.

latency.label: Latency
latency.definition: The time between a request and its response.

memory-footprint.label: Memory footprint
memory-footprint.definition: How much RAM a program needs while it runs.

rag.label: RAG
rag.definition: Retrieval-augmented generation: look up relevant documents first, then give them to a language model to base its answer on.

llm-evaluation.label: LLM evaluation
llm-evaluation.definition: Measuring how good a language-model application's outputs are, often with rubrics, human labels or another model acting as judge.

prompt-engineering.label: Prompt engineering
prompt-engineering.definition: Shaping a language model's behavior by changing its instructions and examples, without changing the model itself.

fine-tuning.label: Fine-tuning
fine-tuning.definition: Further training a pre-trained model on your own examples so that its behavior or style changes.

hallucination.label: Hallucination
hallucination.definition: When a language model states something fluent and confident that is false or unsupported.

ai-agent.label: AI agent
ai-agent.definition: A language-model system that decides for itself which tools to call and which steps to take toward a goal.

tool-calling.label: Tool calling
tool-calling.definition: A model asking for external code to run, such as a search or database query, and then using the result.

json.label: JSON
json.definition: A text format for structured data using key-value pairs and arrays.

token.label: Token
token.definition: A chunk of text, often a word fragment, that a language model reads and generates one at a time.

temperature.label: Temperature
temperature.definition: A sampling setting on LLM requests, usually between 0 and 2.

top-p.label: Top-p
top-p.definition: Another sampling setting on LLM requests, between 0 and 1.

system-prompt.label: System prompt
system-prompt.definition: Instructions given to a language model ahead of the user's input to set its behavior.

chunk.label: Chunk
chunk.definition: A segment of a document split out for indexing and retrieval.

ground-truth.label: Ground truth
ground-truth.definition: The verified correct answers against which a system's outputs are compared.

precision-recall.label: Precision and recall
precision-recall.definition: Precision is the share of predicted positives that are correct. Recall is the share of actual positives that were found.

validation-set.label: Validation set
validation-set.definition: Data held out from training and used to evaluate a model while it is being developed.

random-forest.label: Random forest
random-forest.definition: An ensemble of decision trees, each trained on a random sample of the data, whose predictions are combined.

predicted-probability.label: Predicted probability
predicted-probability.definition: The number between 0 and 1 that a classifier outputs for how likely a case is to be positive.

high-cardinality.label: High cardinality
high-cardinality.definition: Describes a feature with a very large number of distinct values.

multicollinearity.label: Multicollinearity
multicollinearity.definition: When two or more input features are strongly correlated with each other.

decision-threshold.label: Decision threshold
decision-threshold.definition: The score above which a model's output is treated as a positive prediction.

residual.label: Residual
residual.definition: The difference between an observed value and the model's prediction for it.

r-squared.label: R-squared
r-squared.definition: The share of variance in the outcome that a regression model explains.

training-data.label: Training data
training-data.definition: The historical examples a model learns from.

retraining.label: Retraining
retraining.definition: Fitting a model again on newer data to replace the version in production.

psi.label: PSI
psi.definition: Population Stability Index: a score that compares the binned distribution of a variable between two periods.

feature-store.label: Feature store
feature-store.definition: A shared system that stores, computes and serves model input features.

human-review.label: Human review
human-review.definition: A step in which a person checks or overrides a model's output before action is taken.

data-structure.label: Data structure
data-structure.definition: A way of organizing data in memory so it can be accessed or changed efficiently.

dataframe.label: DataFrame
dataframe.definition: A table of rows and labeled columns, as used in pandas.

default-argument.label: Default argument
default-argument.definition: A value a function parameter takes when the caller does not supply one.

parallelism.label: Parallelism
parallelism.definition: Running several computations at the same time on separate CPU cores or machines.

ranking.label: Ranking
ranking.definition: Ordering rows by a value and assigning each a position, such as 1st or 2nd.

aggregate-function.label: Aggregate function
aggregate-function.definition: A function such as COUNT, SUM or AVG that collapses many rows into one value.

growth-rate.label: Growth rate
growth-rate.definition: The change in a metric between two periods, usually shown as a percentage of the earlier period.

streak.label: Streak
streak.definition: A run of consecutive days (or other periods) with the same behavior.

join.label: Join
join.definition: An operation that combines rows from two tables using a matching condition.

null-value.label: NULL
null-value.definition: A marker meaning a value is missing or unknown. It is not the same as zero or an empty string.

median.label: Median
median.definition: The middle value when observations are sorted: half the values fall below it and half above.

repeat-purchase-rate.label: Repeat purchase rate
repeat-purchase-rate.definition: The share of customers who buy more than once.

central-limit-theorem.label: Central limit theorem
central-limit-theorem.definition: A theorem in probability about the averages of samples.

mean.label: Mean
mean.definition: The arithmetic average: the sum of values divided by how many there are.

frequentist.label: Frequentist
frequentist.definition: An approach to inference in which probability describes long-run frequencies across repeated experiments.

causation.label: Causation
causation.definition: A relationship in which changing one variable produces a change in another, rather than the two merely moving together.

control-group.label: Control group
control-group.definition: The subjects who do not receive the treatment, used as the comparison for those who do.

standard-error.label: Standard error
standard-error.definition: A measure of how much a statistic, such as a sample mean, would vary across repeated samples.

anomaly-detection.label: Anomaly detection
anomaly-detection.definition: Identifying observations that deviate markedly from the expected pattern.

scenario-analysis.label: Scenario analysis
scenario-analysis.definition: Examining how an outcome changes under different sets of assumptions.

embedding.label: Embedding
embedding.definition: A list of numbers representing a piece of text (or other data) so that similar items sit close together.

linear-regression.label: Linear regression
linear-regression.definition: A model that predicts a number as a weighted sum of input features.

ridge.label: Ridge regression
ridge.definition: Linear regression with a penalty on the squared size of its coefficients (an L2 penalty).

lasso.label: Lasso
lasso.definition: Linear regression with a penalty on the absolute size of its coefficients (an L1 penalty).

decision-tree.label: Decision tree
decision-tree.definition: A model that makes predictions by asking a sequence of yes-or-no questions about the features.

lightgbm.label: LightGBM
lightgbm.definition: A gradient boosting library from Microsoft.

catboost.label: CatBoost
catboost.definition: A gradient boosting library from Yandex.

support-vector-machine.label: Support vector machine
support-vector-machine.definition: A classifier that separates classes with a boundary chosen using the points closest to it.

support-vector-regression.label: SVR
support-vector-regression.definition: Support vector regression: the regression counterpart of the support vector machine.

k-nearest-neighbors.label: k-nearest neighbors
k-nearest-neighbors.definition: A method that predicts using the labels of the k most similar training examples.

naive-bayes.label: Naive Bayes
naive-bayes.definition: A family of simple probabilistic classifiers based on Bayes' rule.

generalized-linear-model.label: Generalized linear model
generalized-linear-model.definition: A family of models that extends linear regression to outcomes with other distributions, such as counts or yes/no.

isolation-forest.label: Isolation forest
isolation-forest.definition: An unsupervised method for scoring how unusual each observation is, built from random trees.

k-means.label: k-means
k-means.definition: A clustering method that groups points around k center points.

clustering.label: Clustering
clustering.definition: Grouping similar items together without predefined labels.

dbscan.label: DBSCAN
dbscan.definition: A clustering method that groups points by how densely packed they are.

hierarchical-clustering.label: Hierarchical clustering
hierarchical-clustering.definition: A clustering method that builds a tree of nested groups.

gaussian-mixture-model.label: Gaussian mixture model
gaussian-mixture-model.definition: A model that describes data as a blend of several bell-shaped distributions.

pca.label: PCA
pca.definition: Principal component analysis: a technique that rewrites data in terms of new, uncorrelated directions.

t-sne.label: t-SNE
t-sne.definition: A technique for drawing high-dimensional data as a two-dimensional picture.

feature-selection.label: Feature selection
feature-selection.definition: Choosing a subset of the available input features to use in a model.

stacking.label: Stacking
stacking.definition: An ensemble method in which a second model learns to combine the predictions of several base models.

smote.label: SMOTE
smote.definition: Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique: a way of creating artificial examples of a rare class.

hyperparameter.label: Hyperparameter
hyperparameter.definition: A setting chosen before training, such as tree depth, rather than learned from the data.

feature-scaling.label: Feature scaling
feature-scaling.definition: Rewriting features so they sit on comparable ranges.

neural-network.label: Neural network
neural-network.definition: A model made of layers of simple units whose connection weights are learned from data.

backpropagation.label: Backpropagation
backpropagation.definition: The procedure used to compute how each weight in a neural network should change.

gradient-descent.label: Gradient descent
gradient-descent.definition: An optimization method that repeatedly adjusts parameters in the direction that lowers the loss.

learning-rate.label: Learning rate
learning-rate.definition: The size of each update step taken while training a model.

loss-function.label: Loss function
loss-function.definition: A formula that scores how wrong a model's predictions are, which training tries to minimize.

dropout.label: Dropout
dropout.definition: A neural network technique in which random units are switched off during training.

batch-normalization.label: Batch normalization
batch-normalization.definition: A neural network layer that standardizes its inputs across each training batch.

convolutional-neural-network.label: Convolutional neural network
convolutional-neural-network.definition: A neural network that scans small filters across grid-like data such as images.

rnn.label: RNN
rnn.definition: Recurrent neural network: a model that reads a sequence one step at a time, carrying a memory forward.

transformer.label: Transformer
transformer.definition: A neural network architecture built around attention, used by most modern language models.

attention.label: Attention
attention.definition: A mechanism that lets a model weigh how relevant each part of its input is when producing an output.

pretrained-model.label: Pretrained model
pretrained-model.definition: A model already trained on a large dataset, available as a starting point.

tf-idf.label: TF-IDF
tf-idf.definition: Term frequency-inverse document frequency: a score for how characteristic a word is of a document.

word2vec.label: word2vec
word2vec.definition: A method for learning a vector of numbers for each word from large amounts of text.

rlhf.label: RLHF
rlhf.definition: Reinforcement learning from human feedback: training a model using human preferences as a signal.

likelihood.label: Likelihood
likelihood.definition: The probability a model assigns to the observed data, viewed as a function of the model's parameters.

chi-square-test.label: Chi-square test
chi-square-test.definition: A hypothesis test comparing observed counts in categories with the counts expected under no relationship.

multi-armed-bandit.label: Multi-armed bandit
multi-armed-bandit.definition: A method that adaptively allocates traffic among options while learning which performs best.

arima.label: ARIMA
arima.definition: AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average: a classical model for forecasting a single time series.

exponential-smoothing.label: Exponential smoothing
exponential-smoothing.definition: A forecasting method that weights recent observations more heavily than older ones.

prophet.label: Prophet
prophet.definition: An open-source forecasting library from Meta.

mape.label: MAPE
mape.definition: Mean absolute percentage error: the average of absolute errors as a percentage of the actual values.

matrix-factorization.label: Matrix factorization
matrix-factorization.definition: A technique that approximates a large table as the product of two smaller ones.

cosine-similarity.label: Cosine similarity
cosine-similarity.definition: A measure of how alike two vectors are, based on the angle between them.

lora.label: LoRA
lora.definition: Low-Rank Adaptation: a technique for fine-tuning a model by training small added matrices.
